newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Down on poor regional demand.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Down on poor regional demand.

text.p: Singapore light distillates fell amid crude's losses and the absence of regional demand, traders said on Friday.
Pressure from prompt supplies is depressing the naphtha market with Singapore barrels assessed at only 30-40 cents per barrel over spot quotes, compared to $1.00 traded two weeks ago.

Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) bought by tender 28,000 tonnes of naphthenic-and-aromatic (N+A) naphtha for September 11-20 delivery at $208.75 per tonne to a Swiss trader, cost-and-freight (c-and-f) Kaohsiung, industry sources said.
"The award was a little lower than $210," a CPC official said.
The latest award is higher than CPC's previous N+A purchase, for August 15-31 delivery, which was at $196 per tonne, c-and-f basis.
"It is quite low compared to the previous few days on the open-spec," said a trader.
On Friday, two open-spec cargoes for September 1-15 delivery were traded at $209 per tonne c-and-f Japan.
In Singapore, naphtha swaps were also lower with August traded at $21.80 but last quoted at $21.50/$21.60 per barrel, down 35 cents from Thursday. September was talked on par to August.
Regional demand is thin with Taiwan unlikely to re-emerge soon as it has covered its September requirements, the official said.
Traders said the outlook remained bearish amid high stocks in north Asia, resulting in the absence of buyers for September 1-15 and only a few for the second half.
The intermonth (September/October) contango in the open-spec also steepened to $1.50/$1.00 per tonne from 75 cents/even on Wednesday.
"It will continue to weaken.. there are just no buyers," said a trader.
Amid a lack of buyers, gasoline extended its losses by around 30 cents per barrel with the 92-octane offer by a European major down to $$2 .30, fob Singapore, August 16-20 lifting.
A Dutch trader lowered its 95-octane lifting August 18-22 to $23.25 from $23.50 on Thursday.
A trader said a South Korean refiner won Philippines oil refiner Petron Corp's buy tender for 100,000 barrels of 95 or 97-octane unleaded reformate for delivery August 10-20.
No confirmation was available but on Thursday levels were heard around $5 over Singapore naphtha spot quotes on a cost-and-freight basis to Bataan.
The trader said Petron was now seeking September 1-15 cargoes.
(Prices are in dollars per barrel)
